items.summary_full: DoubleLine 首席执行官兼首席投资官 Jeffrey Gundlach 与 Zulauf Asset Management 的 Felix Zulauf 展开了一场由 Grant Williams 主持的广泛宏观经济对话。双方对宏观形势的看法一致：世界正从单极格局向多极格局转型，战争和制裁会造成结构性通胀。此外，市场正处于资本支出和人工智能驱动的上涨周期的后期阶段，Zulauf 先生认为该周期可能在今年第三季度至明年第一季度之间见顶，随后将迎来由经济衰退引发的 30% 至 50% 的熊市。Gundlach 先生对此表示赞同，并补充说，美国股市中人工智能股票的集中度——10 只股票占标普 500 指数的 41%——几乎与以往市场周期的顶部完全吻合，而且美国股市的表现已经开始逊于世界其他地区，他认为这一趋势才刚刚开始。 关于利率和财政前景，冈拉克先生认为，鉴于利息支出已从每年3000亿美元飙升至近1.4万亿美元，且财政赤字持续维持在每年2万亿美元，即使在经济衰退的情况下，美国长期国债收益率也不会出现显著下降。他提出，当经济形势变得严峻时，收益率曲线控制和潜在的国债重组可能是应对政策的措施。他略带讽刺地指出，NEC主任凯文·哈塞特对重组方案的否定，听起来很像华尔街的“绝不可能”。对于私募信贷，冈拉克先生毫不留情地进行了批评，将当前环境与2005年至2006年的情况相提并论，指出当时存在着虚假评级、人为操纵的波动性、隐瞒的软件风险敞口，以及私募股权、私募信贷和离岸再保险之间错综复杂的利益关系，而这些机构缺乏透明度和监管。祖劳夫先生补充说，一些私人信贷公司将会消失，而真正的清算只有在市场转向、浪潮退去时才会到来。 Jeffrey Gundlach and Felix Zulauf: The Second Inning of a Major Shift 22 Jun 2026 LOS ANGELES https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeodaCXCG5w

items.summary_full: 在这段摘自 DoubleLine 9 月于纽约广场酒店（Plaza Hotel）举办的客户活动视频中，首席执行官兼首席投资官 Jeffrey Gundlach 与副首席投资官 Jeffrey Sherman 联袂登台，就债券、信贷及市场走势展开了广泛探讨。Gundlach 先生指出，投资者数十年来所依赖的许多市场关联性已然失效，他将这一新局面称为“反常世界”（backward land）。由此引发的最显著后果，是一种与传统共识相悖的观点：即“在下一次经济衰退期间，长期利率反而会上升”。这是因为经济下行将推动财政赤字逼近 GDP 的 12%，并使年度利息支出向 3 万亿美元大关靠拢。鉴于政府对利率走向日益感到不安，他预计当局将采取更多干预措施，而“扭曲操作”（Operation Twist）的升级版很可能就是第一步。 在信贷领域，Gundlach 先生观察到市场边缘已出现裂痕：人工智能（AI）相关债券的利差大幅走阔，远超市场其他板块；同时，私募信贷资产的估值也引发了实质性疑虑。谈及那些授予债券“投资级”评级的机构时，他直言不讳地表示：“那根本不是分析，那只是价目表。”此外，他还列举了相对安全的投资领域，包括久经考验的证券化信贷产品及新兴市场本币债券；但他同时也提醒投资者，鉴于当前的股票估值水平与市场高度集中的现状，投资容错空间已所剩无几。 Gundlach: Rates, Risk and the Road Ahead https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FADR_Ba2y-0

Jeff Gundlach, "The Bond King" himself, points to oil and bond supply as two culprits behind the selloff. His bigger worry is the trajectory of U.S. debt, now north of $40 trillion, and the risk that policymakers get pushed into something drastic, even a Treasury restructuring. I'm not there yet. I lay the yield spike mostly at Kevin Warsh's feet, since his approach has left the bond market thoroughly confused about where policy is headed. We also sparred over the shape of the next recession. I see a classic risk-off episode sending money straight back into bonds, just as we've seen time and again. Jeff suspects we've entered a new regime where the old relationships no longer hold. Then there's the AI mania, where Jeff reads widening credit spreads as an early warning sign. Is a crisis around the corner? items.summary_full: Jeffrey Gundlach: Fed Needed ‘Stun and Done’ Hike of 50 bps 17 Sept 2026 NEW YORK DoubleLine CEO-CIO Jeffrey Gundlach joins CNBC following Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) press conference, calling the FOMC’s hike of 25 basis points (bps) a case of too little, too late. Mr. Gundlach says he would have dissented in favor of 50 bps, what he dubs “stun and done,” pointing to sustained inflation metrics. He’s skeptical of the Fed’s new subcommittees, comparing them to a struggling business hiring consultants who “always want to figure out what the people at the company really want to hear” rather than deliver hard truths. He also draws a sharp parallel between AI mania today and COVID-19 vaccine guidance, joking that the current mood has shifted from “AI is going to let us all retire and live on Tahiti” to “we’re all going to be dead by the end of the decade.” On markets, Mr. Gundlach flags a widening gap in credit, noting AI-related investment grade (IG) bonds have widened 50 bps in recent months while the rest of the IG market has barely moved. It’s a sign the market simply “does not believe the ratings that are on these AI bonds.” He continues to favor the equal-weighted S&P 500 over the cap-weighted index, sees no reason to buy long-term U.S. Treasuries without a real yield over inflation and remains constructive on emerging markets local currency debt. On the Treasury Department’s expanded bond-buyback program, he isn’t impressed, dismissing it as “kissing your sister” and arguing a much larger effort will be needed to meaningfully move yields. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xusUcwrhPCQ

items.summary_full: Gundlach Unlocked: The Fed’s Next Move 11 Sept 2026 LOS ANGELES DoubleLine CEO-CIO Jeffrey Gundlach’s latest Gundlach Unlocked webcast reviews the macroeconomic landscape heading into next week’s Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Mr. Gundlach remains skeptical that the Federal Reserve will hike rates despite the market pricing a real probability of one, and he warns that a hold could push long-term rates meaningfully higher given persistent inflation pressure. Mr. Gundlach also flags a growing divergence in credit markets, with spreads on AI-related corporate bonds widening sharply even as the broader market holds near its tights for the year. On inflation, he points to several troubling data points, from rising import and export prices to a CPI trajectory Mr. Gundlach says looks eerily similar to the setup that preceded the inflation spiral of the 1970s. On equities, he reiterates his warning about historic market concentration and continues to favor a more equal-weighted approach rather than through the capitalization-weighted S&P 500 Index. He closes bearish on the U.S. dollar and constructive on both emerging markets equities and local currency debt, while he cautions that the U.S. Treasury Department’s newly announced buyback program is unlikely to meaningfully move long-term U.S. Treasury yields. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVwbX7dcQWc

items.summary_full: Jeffrey Gundlach on Channel 11: So Much Said, So Little Heard 4 Aug 2026 LOS ANGELES DoubleLine Portfolio Manager Ken Shinoda welcomes firm CEO-CIO Jeffrey Gundlach for a special edition of Channel 11, recorded the morning after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s second FOMC press conference, which Mr. Gundlach does not mince words about. Citing CNBC’s Steve Liesman, he calls it a case of “so much said, so little heard,” pointing to the 2s30s U.S. Treasury yield curve move from negative 108 basis points (bps) to positive 100 bps as proof the long end is punishing the Fed for talking tough on 2% inflation without acting on it. Mr. Gundlach believes a September hike is now a high-probability outcome, the only real way for Chairman Warsh to “get the stain off” the credibility he spent in this press conference. On positioning, Mr. Gundlach reiterates his long-standing playbook: stay short and up in quality; avoid the long end entirely; and lean into structured products like legacy RMBS and asset-backed securities, which he thinks may now be safer than Treasuries given how much home equity has built up. He’s also more constructive on the plain-vanilla high yield bond market than he’s been in years, arguing that the riskiest borrowers have migrated to private credit and bank loans instead, leaving public junk bonds in comparatively better shape. On private credit itself, he returns to a familiar and pointed example, walking through the math behind a fund’s markdown from 100 to 81 and noting that under any honest scenario, some portion of the portfolio has to be worth close to zero. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XnlBAe7SIGk

items.summary_full: DoubleLine 首席执行官兼首席投资官 Jeffrey Gundlach 与 Zulauf Asset Management 的 Felix Zulauf 展开了一场由 Grant Williams 主持的广泛宏观经济对话。双方对宏观形势的看法一致：世界正从单极格局向多极格局转型，战争和制裁会造成结构性通胀。此外，市场正处于资本支出和人工智能驱动的上涨周期的后期阶段，Zulauf 先生认为该周期可能在今年第三季度至明年第一季度之间见顶，随后将迎来由经济衰退引发的 30% 至 50% 的熊市。Gundlach 先生对此表示赞同，并补充说，美国股市中人工智能股票的集中度——10 只股票占标普 500 指数的 41%——几乎与以往市场周期的顶部完全吻合，而且美国股市的表现已经开始逊于世界其他地区，他认为这一趋势才刚刚开始。 关于利率和财政前景，冈拉克先生认为，鉴于利息支出已从每年3000亿美元飙升至近1.4万亿美元，且财政赤字持续维持在每年2万亿美元，即使在经济衰退的情况下，美国长期国债收益率也不会出现显著下降。他提出，当经济形势变得严峻时，收益率曲线控制和潜在的国债重组可能是应对政策的措施。他略带讽刺地指出，NEC主任凯文·哈塞特对重组方案的否定，听起来很像华尔街的“绝不可能”。对于私募信贷，冈拉克先生毫不留情地进行了批评，将当前环境与2005年至2006年的情况相提并论，指出当时存在着虚假评级、人为操纵的波动性、隐瞒的软件风险敞口，以及私募股权、私募信贷和离岸再保险之间错综复杂的利益关系，而这些机构缺乏透明度和监管。祖劳夫先生补充说，一些私人信贷公司将会消失，而真正的清算只有在市场转向、浪潮退去时才会到来。 Jeffrey Gundlach and Felix Zulauf: The Second Inning of a Major Shift 22 Jun 2026 LOS ANGELES https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeodaCXCG5w

items.summary_full: Sherman Says: The Dirty Secret in the Bond Market 25 Apr 2026 LOS ANGELES In the inaugural episode of DoubleLine’s Sherman Says, Deputy CIO Jeffrey Sherman and Strategist Ryan Kimmel are led by Relationship Manager Nick Dalgety through a discussion of the current macro and market landscape. The focus is on persistent inflation pressures driven by energy price volatility, tariffs and elevated services inflation, which continue to challenge the Federal Reserve’s policy path. From an investment perspective, the group emphasizes disciplined positioning in an increasingly complex fixed-income environment, where starting yield and security selection remain critical. As Sherman notes, “The dirty secret in the bond market is that one of the highest Sharpe ratios almost always sits at the front of the curve. You want to be in things that are shorter in nature, higher quality and more analyzable – especially with an unpredictable policy environment.” The team also highlights relative value opportunities and areas where valuations remain more attractive on a historical basis. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_BwLuCj01_Y
